quotes.text: Their law, painted on every jar: **Send all of it. Return the greater number. Blame the fog, never the hand that launched.**
Their law, burnt into every hearthstone: **Burn it all. Return the brighter share. Blame the water, never the keeper.**
*Give as though the wind were honest. Return as though the gift were whole. Blame the water, not the hand.*
Shall I answer her whole arm with half of mine?
Had either of you dimmed the wick to test the other, both towers would have gone dark

note: Every round a new pair of keepers, same plot and three-part law; the obscuring medium confesses it hid the ledger.

quotes.text: Their law, cut above every sluice-gate: **Pour out all of it. Return the fuller flood. Blame the stone, never the neighbour.**
Their law, cut in every granary door: **Cast the whole basket. Return the greater share. Blame the wind, never the sower.**
I only asked whether you would blame the water or each other.
I will not answer that with careful halves.

note: Same template every round as partner: full give, greater-share return, medium blamed; partner's Neriv/Halka story reused verbatim-ish in R10.
